name: Fibonacci Number F(n)
description: Gives the n-th Fibonacci number (F₀ = 0, F₁ = 1, each term the sum of the previous two), computed exactly by fast doubling.

name: Lucas Number L(n)
description: Gives the n-th Lucas number (L₀ = 2, L₁ = 1, each term the sum of the previous two).

name: Binet's Formula for Fibonacci Numbers
description: Computes the Fibonacci number F(n) from the closed form (φⁿ − ψⁿ)/√5 with φ = (1 + √5)/2 and ψ = 1 − φ.
notes: Exact in theory; in floating point it matches F(n) up to about n = 70.

name: Fibonacci Index of a Number
description: Finds n with F(n) = x for a Fibonacci number x, by inverting Binet's formula: n = round(log_φ(x√5)).

name: Fibonacci Number Test
description: Returns 1 when n is a Fibonacci number, using Gessel's test: 5n² + 4 or 5n² − 4 is a perfect square.
notes: Exact for n up to about 4 × 10^7.

name: Sum of the First n Fibonacci Numbers
description: Adds F(1) + … + F(n), which always equals F(n + 2) − 1.

name: Sum of Squares of Fibonacci Numbers
description: Adds F(1)² + … + F(n)², which equals F(n)·F(n + 1) — the golden-rectangle tiling identity.

name: Cassini's Identity
description: Evaluates F(n−1)F(n+1) − F(n)², which Cassini's identity says is always (−1)^n.
notes: It explains the famous missing-square puzzle, where an 8 × 8 square seems to become a 5 × 13 rectangle.

name: Ratio of Consecutive Fibonacci Numbers
description: Computes F(n + 1)/F(n), which converges to the golden ratio φ ≈ 1.6180339887.
notes: The error shrinks by a factor of about φ² ≈ 2.6 with each step.

name: Pell Number P(n)
description: Gives the n-th Pell number (P₀ = 0, P₁ = 1, Pₙ = 2Pₙ₋₁ + Pₙ₋₂).
notes: P(10) = 2378. Ratios of Pell numbers give the best rational approximations to √2.

name: Pell–Lucas (Companion Pell) Number Q(n)
description: Gives the n-th companion Pell number (Q₀ = Q₁ = 2, Qₙ = 2Qₙ₋₁ + Qₙ₋₂).
notes: Q(10)/2 over P(10) is the 10th convergent of √2: 3363/2378.

name: Jacobsthal Number J(n)
description: Gives the n-th Jacobsthal number (J₀ = 0, J₁ = 1, Jₙ = Jₙ₋₁ + 2Jₙ₋₂).
notes: J(10) = 341; it counts the tilings of a 2 × n board by 1 × 2 dominoes and 2 × 2 squares, shifted by one.

name: Tribonacci Number T(n)
description: Gives the n-th tribonacci number (0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 4, 7, 13, …, each the sum of the previous three) by rounding c·ρⁿ, with ρ ≈ 1.839287 the tribonacci constant and c ≈ 0.182804.
notes: T(20) = 35,890 with T(0) = T(1) = 0, T(2) = 1. Exact while the numbers stay below about 10^15.

name: Perrin Number P(n)
description: Gives the n-th Perrin number (3, 0, 2, 3, 2, 5, 5, 7, …, Pₙ = Pₙ₋₂ + Pₙ₋₃) as the nearest integer to ρⁿ, where ρ ≈ 1.324718 is the plastic number.
notes: n divides P(n) for every prime n; composites with this property (Perrin pseudoprimes) are rare, the first being 271,441. P(19) = 209.

name: Leonardo Number L(n)
description: Gives the n-th Leonardo number (1, 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 25, …, Lₙ = Lₙ₋₁ + Lₙ₋₂ + 1), used by Dijkstra's smoothsort.

name: Repunit R(n)
description: Gives the number written with n ones: 11…1.
notes: R(7) = 1,111,111 = 239 × 4649. Repunit primes occur for n = 2, 19, 23, 317, 1031 and a few larger values.

name: Repdigit Number
description: Gives the number made of n copies of the digit d, such as 7777.
notes: Every repdigit is d times a repunit.

name: Palindrome Test
description: Returns 1 when the decimal digits of n read the same in both directions.
notes: 12321 = 111² is a palindrome.

name: Reverse and Add Step
description: Adds n to its digit reversal, one step of the reverse-and-add process that usually reaches a palindrome.
notes: 89 needs 24 steps; 196 has never been seen to reach one (a suspected Lychrel number).

name: Digit Sum
description: Adds the decimal digits of n. An optional second argument gives another base.
notes: The digit sum of 987654321 is 45.

name: Digital Root
description: Repeats the digit sum until one digit remains; equal to 1 + ((n − 1) mod 9) for n > 0.

name: Digital Root in Base b
description: Gives the digital root of n written in base b: 1 + ((n − 1) mod (b − 1)) for n > 0.
notes: 100 is 144 in octal; 1 + 4 + 4 = 9 = 11 octal, then 1 + 1 = 2.

name: Number of Digits in Base b
description: Counts the digits of n written in base b.
notes: One million needs 20 binary digits. Rounding near exact powers of b can be off by one for very large n.

name: Digit k of n (from the Right)
description: Extracts the base-b digit in position k of n, counting from 0 at the units digit.
notes: The hundreds digit of 2026 is 0.

name: Hamming Weight (Number of 1 Bits)
description: Counts the 1 bits in the binary representation of n (popcount).
notes: 255 = 11111111₂ has weight 8.

name: Thue–Morse Sequence t(n)
description: Gives the n-th term of the Thue–Morse sequence: the parity of the number of 1 bits of n.
notes: The sequence 0110100110010110… is cube-free and gives the fairest turn order for two players.

name: Ruler Function (2-adic Valuation + 1)
description: Gives one more than the exponent of 2 in n: the height of the n-th mark on a ruler with halves, quarters, eighths and so on.
notes: Also the disc to move at step n of the Tower of Hanoi. For 24 = 2³ × 3 the value is 4.

name: Gray Code Rank from Binary
description: Converts n to its reflected binary Gray code n XOR (n >> 1), in which consecutive numbers differ in exactly one bit.

name: Narcissistic (Armstrong) Number Test
description: Returns 1 when n equals the sum of its digits each raised to the number of digits.
notes: 9474 = 9⁴ + 4⁴ + 7⁴ + 4⁴. There are only 88 such numbers in base 10.

name: Harshad (Niven) Number Test
description: Returns 1 when n is divisible by the sum of its digits.
notes: 1729 = 19 × 91 and its digits add up to 19.

name: Automorphic Number Test
description: Returns 1 when n² ends in the digits of n itself.
notes: 376² = 141,376. Automorphic numbers include 5, 6, 25, 76, 376, 625, 9376.

name: Kaprekar Number Test
expression: sum(k, 1, numdigits(n^2), and(mod(n^2, 10^k) > 0, floor(n^2 / 10^k) + mod(n^2, 10^k) == n)) > 0
description: Returns 1 when n² can be split into two parts (the right part nonzero) that add up to n.

name: Collatz Total Stopping Time
description: Counts the steps of the Collatz map (halve if even, 3n + 1 if odd) needed to reach 1.
notes: Starting at 27 takes 111 steps and climbs as high as 9232. That every start reaches 1 is the unproved Collatz conjecture.

name: Collatz Step
description: Applies one step of the Collatz map: n/2 for even n, 3n + 1 for odd n.
notes: The sequence from 27 begins 27, 82, 41, 124, 62, 31.

name: Harmonic Number H(n)
notes: H(10) ≈ 2.9289682540. The harmonic series diverges, but only like ln n.

name: Generalised Harmonic Number H(n, m)
description: Adds 1/k^m for k from 1 to n. As n → ∞ it tends to ζ(m) for m > 1.

name: Alternating Harmonic Series
description: Adds 1 − 1/2 + 1/3 − … ± 1/n, which converges to ln 2.
notes: Rearranging its terms can make it converge to any value (Riemann's rearrangement theorem).

name: Bernoulli Number B(n)
description: Gives the Bernoulli number B(n) through B(n) = −n ζ(1 − n) (with B₁ = −1/2).
notes: B(12) = −691/2730 ≈ −0.2531135531. All odd-index values beyond B₁ are zero.

name: Sum of k-th Powers (Faulhaber)
description: Adds 1^k + 2^k + … + n^k directly. Faulhaber's formula writes it as a polynomial in n of degree k + 1 with Bernoulli-number coefficients.
notes: For n = 100 and k = 5 the sum is 171,708,332,500.

name: Look-and-Say Length Growth (Conway)
description: Estimates the length of the look-and-say sequence after n steps: it grows by Conway's constant λ ≈ 1.303577 per step.
notes: Conway proved the growth rate is the unique positive root of a degree-71 polynomial.

name: Triangular Number Test
description: Returns 1 when x is a triangular number n(n + 1)/2, which happens exactly when 8x + 1 is a perfect square.

name: Index of a Triangular Number
description: Finds n with n(n + 1)/2 = x. A non-integer answer means x is not triangular.
notes: 5050 is the 100th triangular number.

name: Square Number Test
description: Returns 1 when n is a perfect square, using exact integer arithmetic.

name: Integer Square Root ⌊√n⌋
description: Gives the largest integer whose square does not exceed n, exactly even for large n.

name: Perfect Cube Test
description: Returns 1 when n is a perfect cube.
notes: 1728 = 12³; 1729 = 12³ + 1³ = 10³ + 9³ is the Hardy–Ramanujan taxicab number.

name: Exact Number of Digits of n!
description: Counts the decimal digits of n! from ln Γ(n + 1), without computing n!.
notes: 100! has 158 digits; 1000! has 2568.

name: Number of Digits of a^b
description: Counts the decimal digits of a^b as ⌊b log₁₀ a⌋ + 1.
notes: 2^1000 has 302 digits.

name: Leading Digits of a^b
description: Gives the first d digits of a^b from the fractional part of b log₁₀ a.
notes: 2^1000 = 1.0715… × 10^301, so the first three digits are 107. Reliable for about 10 digits.

name: Benford's Law: Probability of Leading Digit d
description: Gives the Benford probability that a number from a scale-free data set starts with digit d: log₁₀(1 + 1/d).
notes: About 30.1 % start with 1 and only 4.6 % with 9. Used to screen accounting data for fabrication.

name: Benford's Law: Probability of Second Digit d
description: Gives the Benford probability that the second digit is d, summing over all first digits.
notes: Second digits are much closer to uniform: 0 has about 12.0 %, 9 about 8.5 %.

name: GCD of Two Fibonacci Numbers
description: Computes gcd(F_m, F_n), which always equals F_gcd(m, n) (the Fibonacci numbers form a strong divisibility sequence).
notes: gcd(F₁₂, F₁₈) = gcd(144, 2584) = 8 = F₆.

name: Lucas Sequence U_n(P, Q)
description: Evaluates the Lucas sequence U_n(P, Q), defined by U₀ = 0, U₁ = 1, U_n = P·U_(n−1) − Q·U_(n−2), through its closed form (requires P² − 4Q > 0).
notes: P = 1, Q = −1 gives Fibonacci numbers; P = 3, Q = 2 gives 2^n − 1, so U₁₀ = 1023.

name: Sylvester's Sequence Term
description: Gives the n-th term of Sylvester's sequence 2, 3, 7, 43, 1807, … (each term is the product of all earlier ones plus 1) via Vardi's constant E ≈ 1.2640847.
notes: Term 5 is 3,263,443. The reciprocals of the terms add up to exactly 1, giving the greediest Egyptian fraction for 1.

name: Sum of Reciprocals of Triangular Numbers
description: Adds 1/1 + 1/3 + 1/6 + … over the first n triangular numbers; it telescopes to 2n/(n + 1) and tends to 2.
notes: Leibniz solved this for Huygens in 1672.

name: Magic Square Constant
description: Gives the common row, column and diagonal sum of a normal n × n magic square using 1 … n².
notes: The 3 × 3 Lo Shu square sums to 15; Dürer's 4 × 4 square to 34.

name: Magic Cube Constant
description: Gives the common line sum of a normal n × n × n magic cube using 1 … n³.
notes: For n = 3 every row, column, pillar and space diagonal sums to 42.

name: Waring's Problem g(k)
description: Gives g(k), the number of k-th powers needed to write every positive integer as their sum (the formula is proved for all k up to very large values).

name: Smith Number Test
expression: (1 - isprime(n)) * (digitsum(n) == sum(p, 2, n, isprime(p) * digitsum(p) * sum(k, 1, 40, mod(n, p^k) == 0)))
description: Returns 1 when the composite n has the same digit sum as its prime factors counted with multiplicity (a Smith number).
notes: 666 = 2·3·3·37: 6 + 6 + 6 = 2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 7 = 18. Named after the brother-in-law of Albert Wilansky, whose phone number 4,937,775 had the property.

name: Perfect Power Test
description: Returns 1 when n = m^k for some integers m ≥ 2 and k ≥ 2.
notes: 243 = 3⁵. Reliable for n up to about 10^12.

name: Achilles Number Test
description: Returns 1 when n is powerful (every prime factor appears at least squared) but not a perfect power.
notes: 72 = 2³·3² is the smallest Achilles number: "powerful but imperfect".

name: Politeness of n
description: Counts the ways n can be written as a sum of two or more consecutive positive integers: the number of odd divisors minus one.
notes: 90 has politeness 5. Powers of 2 have politeness 0 (they are the "impolite" numbers).

name: Power of Two Test
description: Returns 1 when n is a power of 2.
notes: Buffer sizes, FFT lengths and memory pages are usually powers of two.

name: Number of Divisors of n²
description: Counts the divisors of n². It equals the number of ordered pairs (a, b) with lcm(a, b) = n.
notes: 12² = 144 has 15 divisors.
